thread:
aliza.k: noticed a weird spike on staging after last merge, int4 profiles show higher tail latency intermittently

samir: saw that earlier, looked like a cluster of requests at 64-128 tokens, latency jumps ~60ms on some workers

jordan: any flags flipped in the kernel selector? we changed the heuristic last week to prefer fused-dequant kernels for <128 seq

aliza.k: that's what I suspected. but the telemetry shows selection bouncing between fused-dequant and split-dequant on same model + batch size :thinking_face:

mike.r: pinging perf-bot for the profiler dump we triggered during the spike

perf-bot: uploaded profile -> https://artifacts.redwood/profiles/2100001112/trace.tar.gz :file_folder:

samir: downloaded and ran `pprof --proto` quickly. the flamegraph points to `dequant_copy()` inside the hotloop, but also locks in `kv_cache::access()` immediately before

jordan: hmm that suggests contention plus dequant overhead compounding. if kernel selection flips, it may change memory access patterns and cause cacheline traffic
aliza.k: reproduced locally with `RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREF=entropy` and a synthetic workload: `./bench --model x123 --batch 4 --seq 96 --iter 200`

samir: command I used to reproduce: ```bash
GOMAXPROCS=1 ./inference_bench --quant int4 --seq 96 --batch 4 --warmup 20 --runs 100
```

mike.r: ran it with perf: `perf record -g -o perf.data ./inference_bench ...` — stack shows `memcpy`, `dequant_expand`, and `mutex::lock` hotspots
jordan: interestingly, when I force kernel to fused-dequant via `KERNEL_FORCE=fused` the spikes disappear, but accuracy regresses on a small eval set (precision drop ~0.4%)
aliza.k: tradeoff: fused path avoids extra memcpy and mutex churn, better latency; split path preserves numeric stability. problem is the selector oscillating and triggering thrash between code paths
samir: can we make selector stable per-model+shape for N minutes? e.g., sticky choice keying on (model, seq_range, batch_range)
mike.r: quick patch idea: add a simple hysteresis in selector: don't flip unless new kernel is better by >5% median latency over 1k samples. low effort and reversible
jordan: agree as short-term mitigation. long term we should profile why fused gives accuracy drop — possibly quant scale mismatch in kernel reorder
aliza.k: I started a bisect to find the merge that exposed this. first suspect is CL 5432 (scheduler heuristic refactor). bisect state: reverted 2 commits and staging spike went away

samir: can you paste the bisect commands?
aliza.k: `git bisect start HEAD good_commit bad_commit && git bisect run ./tools/run-staging-smoke.sh` — ran on a small pool and found culprit: 5432
mike.r: opened PR to add hysteresis and a telemetry counter to track selector flips per minute: PR https://github.com/redwood/infer/pull/6121
jordan: add an experiment flag `KERNEL_SELECTOR_HYSTERESIS_MS` so we can toggle safely in production during canary
aliza.k: created a follow-up issue #1348 to investigate numeric delta on fused path, assigned to jordan
samir: for rollout: hold the merge 5432 in canary until we land hysteresis + metric dashboards. alerting: if selector flips > 10/min in a host, auto-fail the rollout
mike.r: I'll patch the canary job to include that alert and a perf smoke step. adding to release playbook
aliza.k: thanks. summary: root cause = scheduler heuristic change (CL 5432) that increased entropy in kernel selection for certain shapes -> toggling between fused and split dequant paths -> mem traffic + kv cache lock contention -> intermittent tail spikes + small eval quality regressions. mitigations: revert/hold, add hysteresis, telemetry, investigate numeric gap

jordan: I'll start the numeric checks and add unit tests comparing fused vs split on quant scales
samir: tagging @eng-oncall in case this surfaces during next deploy :eyes:
mike.r: :thumbsup: will follow up with PR and rollout plan
aliza.k: ok moving to update canary notes and adding reproduction steps to the bug - will link perf traces and bisect log in the ticket
